g.text: Both relays off (or both on) = both motor leads on the same rail = stopped and braked.
One relay on = one direction. No relay combination can short the supply.

g.text: How it works (v0.2, frame/README.md safety concept)

FLIGHT: key in, hold CREW POS at FLT. K1 reclines the cradle (only while the pod is UP and latched) until the RECLINED limit opens. Keep holding and pull the release lever: K3 brings the pod down (only while the

cradle is fully reclined on BOTH sides, the lever is held and the safety edge is not pressed) until the pawls drop into the DOWN notch. BOARD: hold BRD + lever: K4 raises the pod; once it is UP and latched, K2 brings the seats upright.

Let go of either hand = stop. E-stop or key out = K0 drops = no motor power at all. Each limit switch is bridged by a 1N5408 so you can always drive back off it (the diode carries the motor current only until the switch re-closes,

~1 s; for actuators drawing > 3 A each use 6A10). Relays: 12 V 30 A automotive SPDT (Bosch type). Wire 14 AWG from the PSU to the bridges, 20 AWG for coils. Test with NOBODY seated: every limit, lock, lever, edge, E-stop, key.
The game shows POD UP / MOVING / DOWN-LOCKED and SEATS UPRIGHT / MOVING / RECLINED from the three sense contacts and announces "pod coming down" over the intercom; it never drives a relay.
